body.statement: For every sequence \(a_n\to\infty\), uniformly over \(\Sigma\in\mathcal K\) with \(\mathcal P(\Sigma)=\{a\}\) and \(\delta_a(\Sigma)\ge a_n/\sqrt n\), \(\Pr_{\Sigma}\{\Gamma_n=\{a\}\}\to1\). More precisely, when \(\delta_a(\Sigma)>2r_n\) and \(\delta_a(\Sigma)>2/n\), the failure probability is at most \(16V/(n\delta_a(\Sigma)^2)\).
body.justification: Coverage becomes informative away from the opposing-sign frontier at the regular covariance-estimation scale.
body.gap: No cited OU paper proves uniform exact-set recovery; generic set inversion does not resolve the nearest-model branch when \(B_n\) is empty.
body.consumer: Analysts obtain a transparent clearance condition under which the honest set collapses to the identified polarity.
